note: Provider acceptance worksheet for the shipped subsets. It separates what the automated synthetic checks already prove from what only a user-approved live run can prove. No account has been connected and no test object has been sent to create these rows: every live field is empty and must be filled by the account owner. Automated results never imply live acceptance, and a fixture cannot fill a live field.
how_to_use: Work one service at a time, and one account at a time, only after the maintainer approves a live acceptance task.
Follow the numbered steps for that service from install through disconnect, and record the outcome of each one.
Use a user-owned token of the documented type with the least permission recorded in connectors/SETUP.md, and record the token type and expiry, never the token itself.
Record the API version in use and the date, because both the wire shape and the reviewed source can change.
Leave case as synthetic unless a real account was really used. A synthetic fixture is never upgraded to live by editing this file.
For an uncertain write, record how it was checked in the service's own UI rather than resending.
If a step fails, record the failure rather than working around it, and leave later live fields empty.

providers.least_permission: An Asana personal access token, which carries exactly the access of the user who created it, so the narrowest reduction is a dedicated account limited to the projects or tasks intended for reading. Asana documents personal access tokens as persistent by default with no documented expiry, so the token must be revoked manually.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /data/gid and label from /data/name, never from the opt-in /data/email
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_project returns gid, name, notes, archived, due_on, owner and permalink_url; read_task returns gid, name, notes, completed, due_on, assignee and permalink_url. Every projected field is one Asana does not mark [Opt In], and no opt-in or html_notes field is projected.
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: none: the profile is read-only, because Asana names the workspace or project in a create body rather than in the path
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked from the same Asana account page

Enable only the read actions this account should offer to tasks.
Run read_project for a project GID taken from an Asana URL and record the returned fields, including whether due_on or owner came back null.
Run read_task for a task GID and record the returned fields.
Not applicable: this profile is read-only.
Not applicable: this profile is read-only.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then deauthorize the token from My Apps and record the revocation date.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/dropbox.json, which reads one folder across the documented /continue cursor route
providers.least_permission: A user access token sent as Authorization: Bearer. The account route is declared auth = user, so app credentials are not accepted. Scope only the folder being read; the spec requires apps to avoid full-Dropbox access.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from /account_id and label from /name/display_name, never from email
synthetic_expectations.read_result: list_folder returns up to three documented pages of entries, following the returned cursor through /2/files/list_folder/continue
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored token; the token is revoked in the Dropbox account's App Console

steps.operation: Install connectors/recipes/dropbox.json and record the app's folder scope.
Connect with a user access token and record the account id and display name.
Enable the account for read access.
Run list_folder on one folder and record the returned entries and whether has_more was true.
Confirm the continuation call used only the returned cursor, and record the second page's entries.
Not applicable: the profile ships two read tools and no upload.
Not applicable: no object is created, so there is no receipt to confirm.
Disconnect, then revoke the token in the Dropbox App Console and confirm Steed asks for reconnection.

providers.engine_bound_note: A reviewed path input is capped at 512 characters by the engine, and a path destination is refused outright, so the shipped subset lists a folder rather than reading one file by its path.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/templates/github-owner-template.json, imported as a user-owned copy with the owner and repository fixed
providers.least_permission: A fine-grained personal access token with a short expiry, repository access limited to the one repository in the reviewed source, and Issues read and write only. No contents, pull request, actions or administration permission, and no account permissions.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /id and label from /login, never from a private email
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_issue returns number, title, state, state_reason and body, with documented nullable fields passed through as explicit nulls, and the same projection for a pull request because the object type is not established
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: POST /repos/{owner}/{repository}/issues with exactly title and body, and a payload_sha256 over the reviewed bytes
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: A create that fails after dispatch is reported as uncertain and never replayed; the repository issue list is checked by hand
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked on the fine-grained tokens page

steps.operation: Copy connectors/recipes/templates/github-owner-template.json, replace the owner and repository placeholders, and import your copy with Add Connector Recipe.
Connect a fine-grained token scoped to that one repository with a short expiry and Issues read and write only. Expect the identity request to return your login.
Enable only the actions this account should offer to tasks.
Run read_issue for a known issue number and record the returned fields, including whether body and state_reason came back null.
Create a draft, review the exact payload, then approve it once. Expect one POST to /repos/{owner}/{repository}/issues with title and body only.
Record the created issue number and URL, then read that issue back to see the stored result. Record explicitly that this confirming read is manual and is not automatic reconciliation.
If the create was uncertain, open the repository issue list in the service UI and record what you found. Do not resend from Steed.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the token on the fine-grained tokens page and record the revocation date.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/gitlab.json, plus connectors/recipes/templates/gitlab-project-template.json imported as a user-owned copy with the numeric project ID fixed
providers.least_permission: A GitLab personal access token with a short expiry. read_api for reads only, or api when reviewed issue creation is wanted, because issue creation is not available to read_api.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /id and label from /username
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_project returns id, path_with_namespace and web_url for one numeric project ID; the per-project template's read_issue returns iid, title, state, description and web_url for one issue IID, with a documented null description passed through as an explicit null and no tier-conditional field projected
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/issues with exactly title and description, a tool description warning that a command starting a line of the description is a quick action, and a payload_sha256 over the reviewed bytes
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: Nothing in this subset can prove a create committed, so the issue list is checked by hand and nothing is resent
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked on the access tokens page

steps.operation: Install connectors/recipes/gitlab.json, or install a copy of the per-project template with your numeric project ID when you want issue reads.
Connect a token with a short expiry and the narrowest scope you need: read_api for reads, api for reviewed issue creation. Expect identity to return your numeric user id and username.
Enable only the actions this account should offer to tasks.
Run read_issue for a known issue IID and record the returned fields, including whether description came back null.
Create a plain draft with no slash command on any line, review the exact payload, then approve it once. Expect one POST to /api/v4/projects/{id}/issues with title and description only.
Record the created issue IID and URL, then read that issue back to see the stored result.

Quick-action subcase: pending unless the account owner has approved one exact non-destructive command in advance. Record the approved command, its expected effect and its cleanup here; otherwise leave pending.
If the create was uncertain, open the GitLab issue list in the service UI and record what you found. Do not resend from Steed.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the token on the access tokens page and record the revocation date.

confirmation.generic_profile: connectors/recipes/gitlab.json stops at the receipt; a person confirms the iid in the GitLab UI.
confirmation.project_template: connectors/recipes/templates/gitlab-project-template.json adds read_issue, so the iid from the receipt is confirmed by a reviewed read.
confirmation.reconciliation: No create tool ships a reconcile step, so nothing polls for the result.

providers.partial_failure_note: A GraphQL query can answer HTTP 200 with data and errors together. Steed reports the errors array rather than returning the partial data as a success.

synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_drive_item returns id, name, webUrl, size and lastModifiedDateTime for both a file and a folder, since the file and folder facets are absent rather than null; the two collection reads return only /value from the first page and never follow @odata.nextLink
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered

Confirm in the source review that the pinned library id is disclosed as user-supplied and unchecked against the account.
Connect a Zotero API key. Expect identity to return your numeric user id and username, and record the value of access.user.library from the response.
Enable the read action this account should offer to tasks.

Not applicable: this template is read-only and offers no write.
Not applicable: this template is read-only, so there is no created object to confirm.

Mismatch check: keep the pinned source unchanged, and run read_item with an item key that belongs to a different library you can access. Expect the service's own failure for an item that library does not contain, and record the exact status. Opening another library in the service does not change what this profile reads.

Alternative mismatch check, only if you want to prove it deliberately: install a second, separately reviewed copy of the template pinned to the other library, connect it as a second account, and record what that copy returns. Disable that second profile afterwards.
Disconnect both accounts if you installed the optional second copy, confirm the credentials are gone, then revoke the key on the API Keys page and record the revocation date.

live_acceptance_preconditions: A maintainer-approved live acceptance task, naming the account, the reviewed source and the permission scope.
A user-owned token supplied by the account owner; no credential is ever committed or pasted into a recipe.
Agreement on what may be created in the real account, and on cleaning it up afterwards.
Confirmation that no completion, delete, administrative or unrelated effect is in scope for any case.
step_order: reviewed draft and write, for services that offer one
receipt and follow-up read, when a write was made
live_fields_may_not_be_filled_from_fixtu: A synthetic result belongs in synthetic_expectations only. Live fields stay empty until an operator explicitly authorizes and completes the steps against a real account.
step_order_note: A read-only service has fewer steps than phases: the write and receipt phases are recorded as not applicable rather than padded with filler.

rules: A phase is recorded only after the phase it requires has been recorded, and no phase after disconnect is ever recorded.
The write and receipt phases apply only where a service offers a reviewed write; a read-only service records them as not_applicable.
A step is bounded: it names one command or one action, and it names the expected outcome rather than leaving it open.
An operation with an effect outside the approved scope stays pending; it is never recorded as performed.
